news.n_may_teotihuacan_burns: Traders from the west say that in the great city of the Sun and Moon, far beyond the mountains, temples and palaces have burned. People say its own inhabitants set fire to their lords’ houses.
news.n_may_caracol_installed: They say the lord of Tikal personally placed a new ruler on the throne of Caracol. Tikal is still master in the east.
news.n_may_copan_moon_jaguar: In Copán a new lord has taken the throne — Tzi Bahlam, Moon Jaguar.
news.n_may_katun_9_6: A k’atun has ended: stelae are raised in the cities and copal is burned, and the daykeepers read prophecies for the next twenty years.
news.n_may_tikal_axes_caracol: Tikal has punished Caracol — they say its lord disobeyed and went over to the Snake kingdom.
news.n_may_lahuntun_559: The priests remind everyone: in five years comes the middle of the k’atun. It is time to prepare gifts.
news.n_may_sky_witness: They say a new lord, Sky Witness, has come to power in the Snake kingdom. Fearsome tales are already told about his warriors.
news.n_may_star_war: Terrible news: Caracol, backed by the Snake, has defeated Tikal! They say Tikal’s lord is dead.
news.n_may_lahuntun_564: The middle of the k’atun: dances and incense in the plazas, and the lords let their blood for the order of the world.
news.n_may_caracol_rises: Traders from the east say Caracol is growing rich on the tribute of the defeated: new temples and hillside terraces are being built there.
news.n_may_copan_rosalila: In Copán a new temple painted red, green and yellow has been dedicated — so bright, they say, that it dazzles the eye.
news.n_may_palenque_kan_bahlam: In Lakamha, in the west, K’an Bahlam I has taken the throne.
news.n_may_katun_9_7: The end of a k’atun: stelae are raised throughout the Maya land, and in every city its lord scatters copal.
news.n_may_chocolate_trade: Traders say that in the south, by the Pacific coast, cacao grows in whole groves and costs half as much as here.
news.n_may_copan_butz_chan: Copán has a new lord — Butz’ Chan, Smoking Sky. People say he is young and fond of building.
news.n_may_jade_motagua: Porters with jade are coming again from the Motagua valley. They say the best jade is the colour of young maize.
news.n_may_yohl_iknal: Unheard of: a woman rules in Lakamha — Lady Yohl Ik’nal.
news.n_may_stones_587: They say the big cities are already preparing stones for stelae for the next k’atun ending.
news.n_may_obsidian_highlands: Obsidian from the southern mountains has grown dearer: the roads are unsafe, and porters only travel in large groups.
news.n_may_katun_9_8: Another k’atun has ended. The daykeepers say the new one will be a time of wars.
news.n_may_caracol_kan: They say Caracol is growing — already bigger than Tikal, if you count all the villages on its hills.
news.n_may_palenque_sacked_599: News has come: the Snake army marched all the way to Lakamha in the west and sacked the city.
news.n_may_ceren_ash: From the south, beyond the mountains, comes a story: a volcano buried a whole village in ash. The people fled in time, but their houses, fields and pots were left under the ash.
news.n_may_pakal_born: A boy has been born to the royal house of Lakamha. He was named Pakal — "Shield".
news.n_may_yohl_iknal_dies: Lady Yohl Ik’nal, ruler of Lakamha, has died.
news.n_may_halley_607: At night a tailed star hangs in the sky. The priests argue whether it means good fortune or war.
news.n_may_palenque_sacked_611: War again in the west: the Snake has sacked Lakamha a second time.
news.n_may_sak_kuk: They say Lady Sak K’uk’ now rules in Lakamha until her son grows up.
news.n_may_katun_9_9: The end of a k’atun: new stelae stand in the plazas, and the nobles dance in the masks of the gods.
news.n_may_pakal_king: In Lakamha a twelve-year-old boy, Pakal, has been placed on the throne.
news.n_may_caracol_kan_ii: K’an II has taken the throne of Caracol. They say he is a loyal friend of the Snake kingdom.
news.n_may_salt_coast: News from the northern coast: the salt pans yielded plenty this year, and the price in the markets has fallen.
news.n_may_lahuntun_623: The middle of the k’atun. Copal burns in the cities, and in the villages the first ears of maize are carried to the altars.
news.n_may_pakal_marries: Pakal of Lakamha has married the noble Lady Tz’akbu Ajaw. The wedding gifts came in a whole caravan.
news.n_may_caracol_naranjo: Caracol has gone to war against Naranjo. They say the eastern roads are dangerous.
news.n_may_copan_smoke_imix: In Copán a new lord has taken the throne — K’ahk’ Uti’ Witz’ K’awiil.
news.n_may_naranjo_falls: Naranjo has been crushed by Caracol and the Snake. They say Naranjo’s lord is dead and the city pays tribute to the victors.
news.n_may_katun_9_10: A k’atun has ended. They say the Snake now has a new capital, Calakmul, from which the world will be ruled.
news.n_may_yuknoom_accedes: Yuknoom Ch’een has taken the throne at Calakmul. His envoys are already travelling across the lowlands.
news.n_may_sak_kuk_dies: In Lakamha Lady Sak K’uk’, who ruled before her son Pakal, has died.
news.n_may_kan_mo_hix_dies: Mourning in Lakamha: K’an Mo’ Hix, father of the lord Pakal, has died.
news.n_may_cacao_pods: Traders complain that hail has damaged the cacao in the south, and the beans have grown dearer.
news.n_may_dos_pilas: They say a young kinsman of Tikal’s king, B’alaj Chan K’awiil, has founded his own city — Dos Pilas, near the Pasión River.
news.n_may_teotihuacan_empty: Traders from the west no longer come with green obsidian. They say the great city of the Sun and Moon has emptied.
news.n_may_katun_9_11: The end of a k’atun. In Copán, they say, the lord has set up stelae all across the valley.
news.n_may_palenque_house_e: In Lakamha Pakal has dedicated a new palace — the White House, where his throne stands.
news.n_may_cancuen_installed: They say Yuknoom Ch’een of Calakmul has placed a lord on the throne of distant Cancuén, at the foot of the mountains.
news.n_may_tikal_flight: News from the north: the Snake army is at Tikal, and King Nuun Ujol Chaak has fled.
news.n_may_nuun_ujol_palenque: They say Tikal’s exiled lord Nuun Ujol Chaak is a guest of Pakal in Lakamha.
news.n_may_lahuntun_662: The middle of the k’atun: in Calakmul, they say, the festival lasted many days, and vassals came from all over the lowlands.
news.n_may_salt_war: They say the owners of the salt pans on the coast have quarrelled — salt has gone up in price again.
news.n_may_feathers: Traders came from the southern mountains with quetzal plumes. The nobles bought them all in a single day.
news.n_may_katun_9_12: A k’atun has ended. They say Tikal has raised its head again and driven its enemies out of Dos Pilas.
news.n_may_tzakbu_dies: In Lakamha Lady Tz’akbu Ajaw, Pakal’s wife, has died.
news.n_may_balaj_exile: They say B’alaj Chan K’awiil, driven out of Dos Pilas, wanders from city to city waiting for help from the Snake.
news.n_may_copan_crowded: People say there are so many people in the Copán valley that fields have climbed to the very tops of the hills.
news.n_may_stela_rumor: An old trader says that in the mountains to the west there are still lords who raise stelae as in the old days.
news.n_may_canoes_coast: They say the northerners’ great sea canoes now travel along the whole eastern coast as far as the southern rivers.
news.n_may_temples_trees: Trees have grown on top of the old temples. Hunters say deer graze in the plazas.
news.n_may_offerings_ruins: Villagers come to the old temples and leave censers of copal there — for the forgotten lords.
news.n_may_new_songs: In the villages people sing new songs — about the Feathered Serpent who came from the west.
news.n_may_dos_pilas_returns: They say the Snake has restored B’alaj Chan K’awiil to Dos Pilas.
news.n_may_dos_pilas_victory: News from Dos Pilas: Tikal’s army has been routed, and B’alaj Chan K’awiil is celebrating victory over his own kin.
news.n_may_naranjo_strikes: Naranjo has taken revenge on Caracol: they say Naranjo’s army reached the enemy’s very walls.
news.n_may_shield_jaguar: In Yaxchilán, on the Usumacinta, Itzamnaaj Bahlam — Shield Jaguar — has taken the throne.
news.n_may_jasaw_accedes: Tikal has a new lord — Jasaw Chan K’awiil. They say he has sworn revenge on the Snake.
news.n_may_six_sky: They say a noble lady from Dos Pilas has arrived in Naranjo — Ix Wak Chan Ajaw, Lady Six Sky. She will rule the city.
news.n_may_pakal_dies: Pakal, the great lord of Lakamha who ruled for almost seventy years, has died.
news.n_may_halley_684: A tailed star is in the sky again. The old people say they saw one like it in their childhood.
news.n_may_kan_bahlam_ii: In Lakamha Pakal’s son, K’inich Kan Bahlam, has taken the throne.
news.n_may_yichaak: Yuknoom Ch’een the Great is dead. At Calakmul Yich’aak K’ahk’ — Fire Claw — has taken the throne.
news.n_may_cross_group: In Lakamha three new temples have been dedicated to the city’s patron gods.
news.n_may_tikal_stela: They say that in Tikal a dated stela has been raised for the first time in over a hundred years.
news.n_may_naranjo_child: In Naranjo a five-year-old boy, Lady Six Sky’s son, has been placed on the throne. His mother rules, of course.
news.n_may_tikal_victory: The news has flown through every city: Tikal has defeated Calakmul! The Snake’s sacred palanquin has been captured.
news.n_may_copan_18rabbit: In Copán the old lord who ruled for sixty-seven years has died. Waxaklajuun Ub’aah K’awiil has taken the throne.
news.n_may_dos_pilas_itzamnaaj: Dos Pilas has a new lord, Itzamnaaj K’awiil. The city is growing rich and building.
news.n_may_xochicalco: Traders from the far west tell of a new city on a mountain whose temple is adorned with feathered serpents.
news.n_may_kan_joy: In Lakamha K’inich K’an Joy Chitam, another of Pakal’s sons, has taken the throne.
news.n_may_yuknoom_took: Calakmul has a new lord — Yuknoom Took’ K’awiil.
news.n_may_comalcalco: They say that on the western coast, where there is no stone, temples are built of fired clay bricks.
news.n_may_kabal_xook: They say that in Yaxchilán Lady K’abal Xook, the lord’s wife, performed a great bloodletting, and an ancestral serpent appeared to her.
news.n_may_tonina_captures: Terrible news from the west: mountain Toniná has captured the lord of Lakamha.
news.n_may_katun_9_14: A k’atun has ended. In Tikal the lord Jasaw has raised a new stela in a "twin-pyramid complex".
news.n_may_copan_temple22: In Copán a new temple has been dedicated with a doorway shaped like the jaws of a mountain monster.
news.n_may_canoe_route: Sea canoes, they say, now sail around the whole peninsula in the north — with salt, honey and cotton.
news.n_may_ahkal_mo_naab: In Lakamha K’inich Ahkal Mo’ Naab, Pakal’s grandson, has taken the throne.
news.n_may_quirigua_king: Copán has seated its vassal K’ahk’ Tiliw Chan Yopaat on the throne of Quiriguá, on the Motagua River.
news.n_may_yaxchilan_temple23: In Yaxchilán Lady K’abal Xook’s temple has been dedicated, with carved lintels finer than any seen before.
news.n_may_piedras_negras: In Piedras Negras, on the Usumacinta, a new lord has taken the throne.
news.n_may_katun_9_15: The end of a k’atun. They say Calakmul raised several stelae at once.
news.n_may_four_capitals: Copán’s scribes have carved the four great kingdoms of the world on a stela: Copán, Tikal, Calakmul and Palenque.
news.n_may_jasaw_dies: Jasaw Chan K’awiil, Tikal’s great lord, has died. His son Yik’in has taken the throne.
news.n_may_wamaaw: They say envoys from Calakmul visited Quiriguá, far to the south. No one quite knows why.
news.n_may_ballcourt_copan: In Copán a new ballcourt has been dedicated, with stone macaw heads along its sides.
news.n_may_rabbit_falls: Unheard of: little Quiriguá has captured the lord of Copán. They say he was executed.
news.n_may_dos_pilas_kawiil: Dos Pilas has a new lord, K’awiil Chan K’inich. They say he is warlike.
news.n_may_shield_jaguar_dies: Shield Jaguar of Yaxchilán, who ruled for sixty years, has died. They say the throne will stand empty for a long time.
news.n_may_tikal_naranjo: Tikal has defeated Naranjo and taken its lord captive.
news.n_may_motul_vases: At the court of Motul de San José, they say, vessels are painted so finely that nobles from the whole region order them only there.
news.n_may_copan_smoke_shell: In Copán K’ahk’ Yipyaj Chan K’awiil has taken the throne. They say he wants to restore the city’s pride.
news.n_may_katun_9_16: The end of a k’atun: Tikal has built another "twin-pyramid complex", and Calakmul new stelae.
news.n_may_bird_jaguar: Yaxchilán at last has a new lord — Bird Jaguar, son of Shield Jaguar.
news.n_may_stairway: They say that in Copán a stairway has been built with glyphs on every step: the whole history of their kings.
news.n_may_cancuen_taj: In Cancuén, at the foot of the mountains, Taj Chan Ahk has taken the throne. They say his palace is larger than any in the lowlands.
news.n_may_halley_760: The tailed star is in the sky again. The priests count the days and whisper with the lords.
news.n_may_dos_pilas_falls: Dos Pilas has fallen: its neighbours took the city, and its nobles fled to the clifftop fortress of Aguateca.
news.n_may_yax_pasaj: In Copán the young Yax Pasaj Chan Yopaat has taken the throne.
news.n_may_kuk_bahlam: In Palenque K’uk’ Bahlam has taken the throne.
news.n_may_tikal_temple_vi: In Tikal a temple has been dedicated with a long inscription carved on its roof-comb, visible from afar.
news.n_may_yax_nuun_ayiin: Tikal has a new lord — Yax Nuun Ayiin II.
news.n_may_ek_balam: From the north, from Ek’ Balam, come tales of a lord building an acropolis with a huge jaw-shaped entrance.
news.n_may_katun_9_17: The end of a k’atun. In Quiriguá, they say, a stela six men tall has been raised — the tallest in the world.
news.n_may_deforest: The old people complain: to find timber for beams and firewood for lime you now have to walk half a day.
news.n_may_altar_q: In Copán an altar has been dedicated showing sixteen kings — from the founder to the present one.
news.n_may_lahuntun_780: The middle of the k’atun. They say even little towns now raise their own stelae and call their rulers holy lords.
news.n_may_palenque_96: In Palenque a tablet of ninety-six glyphs has been carved in memory of the kings — they say the carver’s hand is like the finest scribe’s.
news.n_may_quirigua_kak_dies: K’ahk’ Tiliw of Quiriguá, the conqueror of Copán, who ruled for more than sixty years, has died.
news.n_may_pn_throne: They say a new throne with the faces of ancestors on its back has been dedicated in Piedras Negras.
news.n_may_katun_9_18: The end of a k’atun. More stelae are raised than ever before — but there are more wars, too.
news.n_may_bonampak: They say the palace walls at Bonampak have been painted: a battle, captives and dances — so vivid that the people seem to move.
news.n_may_pn_stela12: In Piedras Negras a stela showing a line of captives has been raised. The wars on the Usumacinta never cease.
news.n_may_palenque_last: They say Janaab Pakal III has taken the throne in Palenque, but his court is poor and the city is emptying.
news.n_may_cancuen_end: Dreadful rumours from the south: enemies have seized Cancuén and the whole royal court has perished. The city is deserted.
news.n_may_drought_rumor: The daykeepers say the rains have grown shorter, and the reservoirs in nearby cities no longer fill to the brim.
news.n_may_walls: They say the cities on the Pasión River are building walls and palisades and hiding their fields behind fences.
news.n_may_yaxchilan_pn: Yaxchilán has captured the lord of Piedras Negras. Since then no stelae have been raised in Piedras Negras.
news.n_may_katun_9_19: The end of a k’atun. Fewer stelae this time: many cities stayed silent.
news.n_may_aguateca_burns: They say enemies burned the fortress of Aguateca. Its people abandoned everything — even the scribes’ paints in the workshops.
news.n_may_puuc_north: From the Puuc hills in the north come tales of rich new cities with stone mosaics on their façades.
news.n_may_migrants: Whole families with bundles are walking the roads north. They say the rains still come on time up there.
news.n_may_lahuntun_820: The middle of the k’atun passed almost unnoticed: copal was burned, but hardly anyone raised new stelae.
news.n_may_copan_end: In Copán, they say, an altar for a new lord was begun — and abandoned. There are no more kings there.
news.n_may_salt_dear: Salt has tripled in price: the trade trails are deserted, and the porters are afraid to travel.
news.n_may_katun_10_0: A great k’atun has ended — the tenth bak’tun of the Long Count has begun. Few cities managed to mark it with a stela.
news.n_may_seibal_watul: They say Seibal, on the Pasión River, has a new lord, Wat’ul — he wears foreign hair and clothing.
news.n_may_chichen_rise: They say that in the north the city of Chichén Itzá is growing, ruled not by one lord but by several brothers.
news.n_may_halley_837: A huge tailed star hangs in the sky, brighter than any before. Many think it is the end of the world.
news.n_may_lahuntun_840: The middle of the k’atun. In Seibal the lord raised stelae; in the old cities there is silence.
news.n_may_empty_courts: People say that in some cities the royal palaces stand empty, and the nobles have gone who knows where.
news.n_may_ramon: A hungry year: in the villages they grind ramón seeds instead of maize.
news.n_may_seibal_four: At the k’atun-ending festival in Seibal the lords of Tikal, Calakmul and Motul gathered — just like in the old days.
news.n_may_katun_10_1: The end of a k’atun. The priests foretell hard years.
news.n_may_north_trade: Traders from the north bring new things: fine orange pottery from the coast and painted cloth in foreign patterns.
news.n_may_abandoned_fields: The fields around the great cities are growing back into forest: there is no one left to work them.
news.n_may_drought_860: They say the drought has lasted several years in a row — even the old people remember nothing like it.
news.n_may_last_scribes: People say that only a few scribes who can read the old inscriptions are left in a whole region.
news.n_may_pilgrims: They say people go to pray at caves and springs rather than at the royal temples.
news.n_may_tikal_last: They say a stela has been raised in Tikal for the k’atun ending. Perhaps the last.
news.n_may_chichen_house: In Chichén Itzá a new building with a long inscription has been dedicated — the north grows rich while the south empties.
news.n_may_uxmal_builds: From the north come tales of Uxmal: palaces are being built there, decorated with masks of the long-nosed rain god.
news.n_may_hamlets: Most people now live in small forest villages. In the former cities only handfuls of families remain.
news.n_may_jimbal: They say a stela has been raised at Jimbal, near Tikal — with foreign-looking figures in the sky.
news.n_may_cacao_north: Cacao is now shipped by sea around the peninsula — the northern traders take all the profit.
news.n_may_seibal_quiet: They say Seibal, too, has stopped raising stelae.
news.n_may_katun_10_3: The end of a k’atun. They say stelae were raised only at Uaxactún, Xultún and Jimbal.
news.n_may_lamanai: People say that in the east, at Lamanai by the lagoon, life goes on as before: they build and trade as if nothing had happened.
news.n_may_roads_overgrown: The white sakbe roads are overgrown: trees already grow on the old road to the neighbouring city.
news.n_may_uxmal_lord: They say the lord of Uxmal, Chaak, has become the most powerful in the north.
news.n_may_chichen_market: Traders say Chichén Itzá has the biggest market they have ever seen, and visitors from the west bring new gods there.
news.n_may_halley_912: The tailed star is in the sky again. The old people recall that their grandparents saw it when the cities were still full of people.
news.n_may_forest_returns: They say jaguars sleep on the temple steps in the old city.
news.n_may_chichen_feathered: News from the north about Chichén Itzá: the Feathered Serpent, K’uk’ulkan, is worshipped there.
news.n_may_old_tales: The old people tell their grandchildren about kings who spoke with the gods — and the children listen as if to a fairy tale.
news.n_may_tula: Traders from the far west speak of a great new city — Tollan, ruled by warriors of the Feathered Serpent.
